validated_results.title: Polymorphisms of glutathione S-transferase μ and θ, MDR1 and VEGF genes as risk factors of bladder cancer: a case-control study.
validated_results.reason: The study examines GSTM1/GSTT1, MDR1 and VEGF genotype distributions as bladder cancer risk factors, providing no population-wide nutritional glutathione exposure estimate.

validated_results.title: Smoking and polymorphisms in folate metabolizing genes and their effects on the histological stage and grade for bladder tumors.
validated_results.reason: Exposure is polymorphisms in folate-metabolizing enzyme genes (MTHFR, MTR, MTRR, TYMS) related to tumour stage and grade, not folic acid intake or status with bladder cancer incidence.

validated_results.title: Nrf2: control of sensitivity to carcinogens.
validated_results.reason: This is a narrative review of Nrf2-mediated chemoprevention mechanisms in rodent models rather than an original human study.

validated_results.title: Fluid intake and incidence of renal cell carcinoma in UK women.
validated_results.reason: Prospective UK cohort of women reporting adjusted relative risk of incident renal cell carcinoma for alcohol intake.

extraction.population: Women in the Million Women Study

sample_size.excerpt: After an average of 5.2 years of follow-up, 588 cases of renal cell carcinoma were identified among 779,369 women.

cases.excerpt: After an average of 5.2 years of follow-up, 588 cases of renal cell carcinoma were identified among 779,369 women.

effect_size.excerpt: While alcohol intake was associated with a reduced risk of renal cell carcinoma (RR for ≥ 2 vs <1 drink per day: 0.76; 95% CI: 0.61-0.96; P for trend=0.02), there was no association with total fluid intake (RR for ≥ 12 vs <7 drinks per day: 1.15; 95% CI: 0.91-1.45; P for trend=0.3) or with intakes of specific beverages.

confidence_interval.excerpt: While alcohol intake was associated with a reduced risk of renal cell carcinoma (RR for ≥ 2 vs <1 drink per day: 0.76; 95% CI: 0.61-0.96; P for trend=0.02), there was no association with total fluid intake (RR for ≥ 12 vs <7 drinks per day: 1.15; 95% CI: 0.91-1.45; P for trend=0.3) or with intakes of specific beverages.

comparison.excerpt: RR for ≥ 2 vs <1 drink per day

design.excerpt: a large prospective cohort of UK women

timing.excerpt: After an average of 5.2 years of follow-up

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Information on beverage consumption was obtained from a questionnaire sent ∼3 years after recruitment

extraction.p_value_method: two-sided Wald test from effect and 95% CI on the log scale
extraction.ethnicity_basis: NA: no field-specific ethnicity evidence was available
